title: Consequence of blending two natures
english: If two natures of different substance have been blended into one mixture, neither one is preserved; instead, both are confused and destroyed.
translator_notes: The Greek text is a fragment that begins mid-sentence. The phrase 'τυγχάνουσαι' is a present active participle meaning 'happening to be' describing the natures. The sentence ends with a period, indicating a complete thought within the fragment.
baehrens: PG 77; Epistula ad Photium ep open
orientation: Cyril of Alexandria writes to Photius, a presbyter of Alexandria, and states a conditional argument about what follows if two natures are blended into one mixture.
